alert_assessment.impact: No user-facing impact yet: 2,908.9 req/s on the websecure entrypoint with 0.18% 5xx and no restarts. The reduced capability is redundancy - all five ingress allocations sit at 89.8-96.7% of the same 4,096 MiB cap, so losing the node that carries about a third of traffic would push the remaining four toward the same wall.
alert_assessment.cause: Traefik's working set scales with in-flight connection and request state, and the 4,096 MiB cap set on 2026-06-24 in f4734b8d is now the binding constraint. On nomad-hst01 memory grew 548.8 MiB in one hour while its request rate went 426.3 to 989.3 req/s; goroutines rose 7,417 to 52,794 and Go heap in use rose 805 MiB. Heap grew faster than the connection count, so a leak component on top of the load-driven growth is not excluded.
alert_assessment.immediate_action: Raise the traefik task memory cap in terraform/environments/va1/nodes/nomad/jobs/ingress/traefik.nomad.hcl and roll the job. The update stanza's max_parallel = 1 with min_healthy_time 30s takes one node at a time, and the anycast health gate withdraws only that node's /32 while it restarts. Host RAM is not a constraint: 376.4 GiB per node with about 296 GiB free on the tightest.
alert_assessment.verification: One hour after the roll, every traefik allocation reports (RSS + swap) / limit below 70% and Total Restarts stays 0.
alert_assessment.long_term_solution: Size the cap against peak per-node ingress rather than a fixed 4 GiB, add memory_max so short spikes oversubscribe instead of OOM-killing, and capture a Go heap profile at high RSS to settle whether growth beyond the connection count is a real leak.

topology: VA1 has five bare-metal Nomad nodes, nomad-hst01 through hst05; hst01, hst03 and hst05 are Raft servers and every node also runs a Nomad client, so servers carry workloads too.
Each VA1 node has 404,156,841,984 bytes of RAM (376.4 GiB); task memory caps are Nomad cgroup ceilings, not host constraints.

traefik is a Nomad system job with one allocation per client binding host ports 80, 443, 9080 (metrics), 8080 (dashboard) and 8081 (tsserve), fronted by a BGP-anycast /32 that lb-anycast-healthgate.service adds or removes based on local Traefik health, so a dead Traefik withdraws that node's route within seconds instead of blackholing.
ECMP across the five anycast nodes is uneven: nomad-hst01 carried 989.3 of about 2,909 websecure req/s while nomad-hst05 carried roughly 317 req/s.
TFC workspace tenant-infra maps to terraform/environments/production; va1-apps maps to terraform/environments/va1/apps; bunnycdn maps to terraform/environments/bunnycdn.

terraform/versions is a shared module consumed by both terraform/environments/production and terraform/environments/va1/apps, so one image-tag bump fans out to tenant-infra and va1-apps in parallel with no cross-workspace ordering.

Grafana at grafana.tailexample.ts.net allows anonymous read of its alert, datasource, provisioning and datasource-proxy APIs, which reaches both VictoriaMetrics and VictoriaLogs; app.terraform.io returns 401 without a token from this session.
decisions: Judge an image bump by the commit range it carries, not by the Terraform diff, which is always a one-line tag change.
Treat a per-workspace result as scoped to that workspace; do not generalise a va1-apps success or failure to tenant-infra for the same commit.
Judge whether a deploy landed by observing the running workload version, not by a Run Applied notification.
Do not infer user impact from a Terraform result or from scheduler state alone.
Before treating a host alert as real, check whether the instance label carries more than one node_uname_info series; a duplicate scrape target inflates rate() and increase() without bounds.
Sanity-check a saturation ratio against physical limits: a value above 1.0 for a link-speed ratio means the metric is wrong, not the hardware.
For a per-allocation threshold alert on a fleet-wide job, check every allocation's ratio before accepting a resolve notice; the condition can move between nodes instead of clearing.

knowledge.subject: VA1 traefik memory cap
knowledge.statement: The VA1 traefik Nomad system job declares memory = 4096 MiB with no memory_max, so 4,096 MiB is a hard cgroup ceiling per node. The cap was raised from 1 GiB to 4 GiB on 2026-06-24 in commit f4734b8d, and by 2026-08-16 all five allocations sat at 89.8-96.7% of it with under 10 KiB of reclaimable file cache and no swap, so the cap is again the binding constraint rather than host RAM.

knowledge.subject: VA1 anycast ingress health gating
knowledge.statement: Each VA1 node advertises the ingress anycast /32 from an lb-anycast dummy interface, and lb-anycast-healthgate.service adds or removes that address based on local Traefik health, so a Traefik that dies or is restarted withdraws its own BGP route within seconds and ECMP re-hashes to the remaining nodes instead of blackholing. Restarting one Traefik allocation therefore drops that node's in-flight connections but does not strand traffic.

knowledge.subject: Per-allocation threshold alerts on fleet-wide jobs
knowledge.statement: When a per-allocation threshold alert on a Nomad system job reports RESOLVED, check every allocation's ratio before accepting it. On 2026-08-16 the VA1 OOM-risk alert cleared only because nomad-hst01 dipped 0.6 points under the 95% line while nomad-hst04 rose above it and nothing restarted, so the condition moved between nodes rather than clearing.

knowledge.subject: VA1 Elixir deploy path
knowledge.statement: elixir_global_version in tenant-infra terraform/versions/elixir.tf is a tenant-backend commit SHA, and terraform/versions is shared by terraform/environments/production and terraform/environments/va1/apps, so a one-line Elixir bump is a code deploy of tenant-backend that fans out to both the tenant-infra and va1-apps workspaces at once.

knowledge.subject: VA1 Nomad deployment healthy deadline
knowledge.statement: VA1 application allocations use min_healthy_time of 10s against a healthy_deadline of 3m0s. An allocation that does not report healthy in that window is marked Alloc Unhealthy, Nomad rolls it back to the previous image, and the Terraform apply that registered the job fails with exit 1.

knowledge.subject: node-exporter instance labelling in VA1
knowledge.statement: The va1-observability node-exporter scrape job takes the instance label from the Consul node name but builds the target address from the Consul service address, so a nomad-client registration advertising a loopback address creates an extra target that scrapes the VictoriaMetrics host under a different node's instance label, producing physically impossible rate() values.

knowledge.subject: VA1 Pure namespace attachment
knowledge.statement: The Pure FlashArray NVMe/TCP namespaces nvme0n14 and nvme0n17 are attached on all five VA1 Nomad nodes but sit at 0 IOPS on every node that is not actively hosting their consuming workload, so non-zero I/O on exactly one node identifies where that workload is placed.

knowledge.subject: VA1 Terraform run diagnosis without HCP access
knowledge.statement: When the HCP Terraform API is unavailable, a va1-apps run can still be reconstructed from inside the cluster: VictoriaLogs service:tfc-agent carries the run id, plan and apply timings and the terminal exit status, and service:nomad carries the allocation and task events that explain which resource failed.

completion.message:
Traefik ingress did not recover. The rule cleared because nomad-hst01 drifted to 94.4% of its memory cap, 0.6 points under the 95% line — nothing restarted, and nomad-hst04 is now higher at 96.7%, sitting about 576 KiB below its hard 4 GiB cgroup limit with almost no reclaimable cache. Traffic is still fine: 2,909 req/s on the public entrypoint with 0.18% 5xx.

All five ingress allocations are between 89.8% and 96.7% of the same cap, so the fleet can't absorb losing one — nomad-hst01 alone carries about a third of the traffic. Memory tracks load (that node went 426 → 989 req/s in two hours, +549 MiB in the last hour), and the 4 GiB cap set back in June is now the binding constraint. Raise it and roll the job; the update stanza rolls one node at a time behind the anycast health gate, and the hosts have 376.4 GiB RAM with roughly 296 GiB free on the tightest. Success check: every allocation under 70% an hour after the roll, with no restarts.

completion.summary: VA1 traefik ingress is saturating its 4,096 MiB per-node cap on all five nodes; the alert cleared only because the condition moved from nomad-hst01 to nomad-hst04. No user impact yet, but redundancy is gone. Raise the cap and roll the job.
material_gaps: No Go heap profile was captured, so the split between load-driven growth and a genuine leak is unresolved; either way the cap is the binding constraint.
